name: Ho Chi Minh City
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Ho Chi Minh City: supplier and partner diligence, M&A research, and arbitration and enforcement support.
hero_lede: Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's commercial capital, its stock market centre and, since the 2025 merger, a manufacturing and port region of some 14 million people. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating qualified local professionals and Vietnamese counsel where local work is required.
intro: Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's largest economy. On 1 July 2025 it merged with Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces, creating a city of more than 14 million people across about 6,772 square kilometres. In 2025 its output was estimated at around USD 120 billion, about 23.5 per cent of national GDP, with growth of 8.03 per cent. The enlarged city combines the services, finance and retail core of the former city with Binh Duong's export manufacturing and foreign-invested industrial base and Ba Ria-Vung Tau's deep-sea ports and energy sector. It hosts more than half of Vietnam's start-ups and, under a 2025 National Assembly resolution, part of the new Vietnam International Financial Centre.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Ho Chi Minh City because it is where much of Vietnam's foreign investment, export manufacturing and deal activity takes place. Buyers relocating supply chains need assurance that factories and suppliers are who they claim to be and meet labour, environmental and trade compliance expectations. Investors acquiring Vietnamese companies need to understand nominee arrangements, related-party dealings and land use rights. Real estate and banking sectors in the city have seen high-profile fraud prosecutions, which raise integrity questions about counterparties. Disputes with Vietnamese parties increasingly lead to arbitration or enforcement proceedings that require evidence about people and assets in the city.

matters.title: Factory and supplier verification
matters.text: Buyers sourcing from the industrial parks of former Binh Duong and the wider city need to know that a supplier exists, owns or leases its facility, and is not subcontracting undisclosed work. We combine enterprise registration data, public records, media and coordinated site enquiries to verify claims.

matters.title: M&A and joint venture diligence
matters.text: Vietnamese companies in the city may be held through nominees, family members or affiliated firms, and depend on land use rights and licences. We map ownership and related parties, review litigation and enforcement history, and identify integrity concerns that affect valuation and deal structure.

matters.title: Real estate and banking counterparties
matters.text: Ho Chi Minh City's property and banking sectors have been at the centre of large fraud prosecutions. Before lending to, investing with or acquiring from developers or financial groups, clients need to understand connected parties, prior proceedings and reputational exposure. We research these from public sources and Vietnamese-language media.

matters.title: Distributor and agent integrity checks
matters.text: Foreign brands entering Vietnam often appoint distributors, agents and customs brokers based in the city. We examine ownership, connections to officials or state-owned enterprises disclosed in public sources, prior disputes and reputational issues, supporting anti-corruption compliance before appointment.

matters.title: Arbitration and enforcement support
matters.text: Disputes with Vietnamese counterparties are frequently arbitrated, and awards may need enforcement in the city. We support counsel by identifying assets, connected companies and the people behind the debtor, and by preparing chronologies and witness backgrounds for proceedings.

local_context.title: Courts in Ho Chi Minh City
local_context.text: The Ho Chi Minh City People's Court hears first-instance commercial disputes above the regional courts' jurisdiction and appeals from them. Since 1 July 2025 it is one of only three provincial courts, with Hanoi and Da Nang, authorised to hear applications to set aside arbitral awards. A 2025 reform replaced district courts with Regional People's Courts, which now handle interim measures and other arbitration-support functions. Judgments are published selectively, so litigation searches are incomplete.

local_context.title: Arbitration in the city
local_context.text: The Vietnam International Arbitration Centre, Vietnam's leading arbitral institution, administers many disputes involving parties in Ho Chi Minh City; it received 532 new cases in 2025 and adopted new rules effective 1 July 2026. Under the 2025 resolution establishing the Vietnam International Financial Centre, a decree created an international arbitration centre within the Centre, whose awards parties may agree not to challenge before Vietnamese courts, a departure from the 2010 Law on Commercial Arbitration.

local_context.title: International Financial Centre
local_context.text: Resolution No 222/2025/QH15 established the Vietnam International Financial Centre, with Ho Chi Minh City as a principal location and Da Nang as a second. The Centre is intended to attract international capital, fintech and financial services with special legal and dispute-resolution arrangements. Its regime is new and implementing rules are still developing, so the status of entities licensed there should be checked case by case.

local_context.title: Registries and land records
local_context.text: Enterprises in the city are registered with the municipal business registration authority, and basic information on name, enterprise code, legal representative and registered capital is available through the national business registration portal. Shareholder detail is limited and filings may require local retrieval. Land use rights are recorded by city land registration offices and are not openly searchable by name, so property research relies on counsel and lawful document requests.

local_context.title: Post-merger administrative changes
local_context.text: The 2025 merger and Vietnam's wider abolition of district-level government changed addresses, administrative units and the offices holding records. Companies formerly in Binh Duong or Ba Ria-Vung Tau now fall under Ho Chi Minh City authorities, and older documents may cite superseded names. Research on entities and property in the region must reconcile old and new administrative references to avoid missing records.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Ho Chi Minh City and works on these matters from Nashville. We begin with the client's purpose and Vietnamese counsel's advice, whether supplier verification, an acquisition, an arbitration under VIAC or Financial Centre rules, or enforcement, and scope the work to it. Sources include business registration data, published court decisions, regulatory announcements and Vietnamese-language media, reconciled for the 2025 administrative changes. Where site visits or local enquiries are needed, we coordinate qualified local professionals under counsel's direction, with attention to Vietnam's 2025 Law on Personal Data Protection. We do not use pretexting or obtain non-public state records. Reports state sources and confidence so clients can act on them in compliance and legal decisions.

faqs.q: Which court hears challenges to arbitral awards made in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Since 1 July 2025, applications to set aside arbitral awards are heard only by the provincial People's Courts of Hanoi, Da Nang and Ho Chi Minh City. For awards involving the city, the Ho Chi Minh City People's Court is usually the relevant court. Regional People's Courts handle interim measures and some other support functions. Vietnamese counsel should confirm jurisdiction in each case.

faqs.q: What is the Vietnam International Financial Centre?
faqs.a: It is a financial centre established by National Assembly Resolution 222 of 2025, located principally in Ho Chi Minh City with a second site in Da Nang. It offers special arrangements for financial businesses and its own international arbitration centre. Because the regime is new, we verify each counterparty's actual status within it rather than relying on claims.

faqs.q: How do you verify a factory in former Binh Duong?
faqs.a: We confirm registration details and legal representatives from business registration data, check addresses against the post-merger administrative units, review media and dispute records, and where needed coordinate a site visit by qualified local professionals. We test whether production capacity, ownership and workforce claims are consistent with what can be observed and documented.

faqs.q: Can company shareholders in Ho Chi Minh City be identified from public records?
faqs.a: Only partly. Public business registration data shows the enterprise code, legal representative and registered capital, but shareholder detail is limited, and nominee arrangements are common. We combine registration information with filings, court decisions, media and connected-entity research to assess likely control, and state how confident each attribution is.

faqs.q: Does the 2025 merger affect company and property research?
faqs.a: Yes. Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau were merged into Ho Chi Minh City on 1 July 2025, and district-level government was abolished. Addresses, administrative units and record-holding offices changed, and older documents may use superseded names. We reconcile old and new references so that relevant records are not overlooked.
